subject: Hosted API pricing — unit-price window & peak QPS scan
messages:
From: Sophie Li <sophie@nimbuslabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amit Patel <amit@brightbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + quick pricing talk

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful overview. A couple of clarifying points from our side so we can align internally:

- Expected steady-state: ~120,000,000 tokens/month (text generation + light embeddings for search indexing).
- Spike behavior: an expected promotional spike that could push short windows to ~1,600 TPS (10-minute bursts, once every few days).
- Budget: finance is looking for an anchoring $/1M target in the $3.50–$4.50 range for committed volume; open to one-off higher rates for short-term excess.

Can you send a few pricing band scenarios (committed slabs + burst pricing) and confirm whether prefix caching helps reduce the billed token count for our use pattern? Also curious about what SLA you can commit to for 99th latency at peak TPS and whether there's a separate premium for geo-failover.

Sophie
Head of Platform — Nimbus Labs

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie@nimbuslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — unit-price window & peak QPS scan

Thanks Sophie — great summary. Quick recap from our end and a proposal for next steps below.

Recap / immediate notes:
- Baseline monthly tokens: 120M (we'll model three committed slabs: 50M, 100M, 200M).
- Peak short-window TPS: 1,600 TPS for ~10 minutes; we'll validate burst handling and whether dedicated burst pool or on-demand serve is better.
- Target $/1M: noted $3.50–$4.50 range as your preferred anchor.

Proposed pricing sketches (attached: redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx):
- Option A (Conservative commit): 50M/month @ $5.25 per 1M, excess billed at $7.75 per 1M; burst buffer (up to 2x baseline TPS) included with 30% throttling grace.
- Option B (Balanced commit): 100M/month @ $4.10 per 1M, excess at $6.25; short-window bursts up to 1,600 TPS handled by automatic burst capacity, small surcharge during cross-region failover.
- Option C (Aggressive commit): 200M/month @ $3.60 per 1M, excess at $5.50; includes prioritized scheduling and 99th-pct latency objective of 250ms for gen calls at burst levels.

Notes on billing & technicals:
- We bill tokens consumed (input + output) at per-1M granularity. Prefix/KV caching reduces compute but currently does not reduce billable token count in hosted plans unless you opt into our cache-aware billing pilot (we can add you).
- For the burst profile you described, Option B typically balances unit cost and flexibility; Option C drives best unit economics but requires a larger commit.

Next steps:
1) We'll drop a filled mutual action plan (MAP) + pricing workbook into Drive by EOD Nov 12.
2) Karthik to validate runbook for 1,600 TPS bursts and confirm whether auto-burst or dedicated pool is recommended.
3) Sophie — confirm which two economics scenarios you'd like modeled (e.g., B + C or A + B).

I'll also propose a 30-minute follow-up on Monday to run through the workbook. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Li <sophie@nimbuslabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — unit-price window & peak QPS scan

Sophie — quick technical note on the burst behavior you called out:

- 1,600 TPS sustained across a 10-minute window is within what our auto-burst subsystem can absorb for non-dedicated customers, but it depends on concurrent KV cache hit-rate and request shape (avg tokens per request).
- For safety we recommend provisioning a short-term reserved burst allocation (100–200 GPUs equivalent) for predictable promotional spikes; that reduces throttling risk and helps preserve the 99th-pct latency objective.
- If most calls are templated (high repetition), prefix/KV caching can cut compute and effective latency dramatically — we can run a quick sample to estimate token reduction.

I pushed a runbook draft and a simple cost calculator to the Drive link in the MAP. Marissa — I flagged the cells that assume 25 tokens/req avg and that 15% of traffic will be short-window promotional spike. Sophie — if you have real request-size telemetry we can replace assumptions.

Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Li <sophie@nimbuslabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Amit Patel <amit@brightbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — unit-price window & peak QPS scan

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the options — this is helpful. Quick replies:

- Model choices: please run scenarios for Option B and Option C (100M and 200M commits). Finance prefers to see the delta at our baseline 120M and an aggressive 200M.
- Cache-aware billing: yes please add us to the cache-aware billing pilot; if that reduces effective billed tokens it's a strong win for us.
- Pilot: we'd like a 6-week pilot for the first tranche (target: 10M trial tokens, proving 1,600 TPS window handles without SLA incidents).

Next steps for teams:
- Marissa: send calendar for Monday follow-up (30m) — we'll slot in product and finance.
- Karthik: run the cost calculator with 25 tokens/req and also with 35 tokens/req to show sensitivity.
- Rishi: can you draft the SLO language for 99th-pct latency at Option B/C levels so procurement can review?

We'll aim to have a procurement decision by Nov 30. Attaching our standard security questionnaire in a follow-up.

Thanks — Sophie
Head of Platform — Nimbus Labs
